r0-context.title: Load baseline context
r0-context.imperative: Read docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, the handoff, the diff, and the relevant packet. Record pass when loaded.
r0-context.finding: Loaded CREW_CONTEXT, GLOSSARY, both handoffs, implementer result, both scripts in full, src/utils/utilization.py (run_jobs mechanism), both new + both modified test files, and full git diff. NOTE: scripts/ has NO __init__.py — spawn-import path needs empirical verification.

r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: Both scripts adopt run_jobs under --utilization (default balanced); build_rolling preserves collect-and-continue (fail_fast=False, worker self-collects) + exit code; rt-comparison preserves fail_fast=True + [default,trained] input-order assembly + unchanged manifest resolution and downstream artifacts. All close criteria met.

r2-scope.title: Scope drift
r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect specific exclusions? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r2-scope.finding: Only the 2 scripts + their 4 test files touched (git status matches handoff). Exclusions verified untouched: src/utils/utilization.py and src/evo_predictor/gold_cycle/ have zero diff. No script output artifact/filename/ordering/exit-code change. Reviewer added 1 real-spawn regression test to the in-scope new test file (handoff explicitly invited it).

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Reproduced independently: pytest over 3 existing + 2 new parallel files = 86 passed (matches handoff). Simplification --paths on the 2 scripts = exactly 1 pre-existing violation (run_comparison=134; AST-confirmed it was 135 on HEAD pre-G5, so reduced by 1, NOT worsened); build_rolling clean. Evidence genuinely demonstrates behavior.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Meets inherited CREW rules: reuses run_jobs util (no duplication), descriptive input validation, test-led (TDD 16-red->87-green), print() acceptable in CLI scripts, no mutable module state added, no DB/FastF1 concerns. All 5 appended constraint checks pass.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: No architecture divergence requiring reconciliation: scripts now consume the shared utilization core (issue #356 intent), honoring one-canonical-path. No docs/contracts/schema changes. Pre-existing run_comparison over-length (134>100) is the only out-of-scope item — already a known triage candidate; not introduced by G5.

r4-spawn-safety.title: PRIMARY: real multi-process spawn safety
r4-spawn-safety.imperative: Workers module-level + spawn-safe; REAL 2-worker ProcessPoolExecutor smoke proves pickling + child execution.
r4-spawn-safety.finding: RAN A REAL 2-WORKER SPAWN SMOKE. Both workers are module-level (brc line 158, rsrc line 341) with heavy/CLI work only under __main__ guard; no import-time side effects. Scripts import as scripts.<module> (Py3.14 namespace pkg, no __init__.py needed); workers resolve by qualified name scripts.build_rolling_compound_priors._rolling_prior_job_worker / scripts.run_sampled_runtime_comparison._backtest_job_worker. Probe via that package path with n_workers=2 ProcessPoolExecutor over REAL (un-mocked) jobs: brc worker executed in-child, caught RuntimeError, returned tagged {ok:False}; rt worker executed in-child and propagated as JobExecutionError under fail_fast=True. Added a guarded, non-flaky pytest regression (TestRealSpawnSmoke, ~3.7s, 3x green). NO spawn defect.

r4-input-order.title: Input-order result assembly
r4-input-order.imperative: run_jobs returns results in input order; build_rolling partitions in round order; rt assembles [default,trained].
r4-input-order.finding: run_jobs reassembles by submission index (utilization.py 266/287). Real-spawn probe submitted rounds out of order (3,1) and got back [3,1]. build_rolling built/failed partition iterates results (round order); rt assembles default,trained=run_jobs([default,trained]) in input order.

r4-picklable.title: Jobs carry only picklable payloads
r4-picklable.imperative: Job dicts carry primitives/paths/dataclass/Namespace that pickle across spawn.
r4-picklable.finding: build_rolling job dict: ints, list[int], Path, frozen CompoundPriorFitConfig dataclass, int — all picklable (proven: real spawn succeeded). rt job dict: argparse.Namespace (picklable), str manifest, Path output, str timestamp — proven picklable via real spawn.

r4-simplification.title: Simplification: no new violation
r4-simplification.imperative: Only pre-existing run_comparison fails; build_rolling clean.
r4-simplification.finding: py -m src.utils.simplification_limits --paths on both scripts: 1 violation only — run_comparison=134 (pre-existing; HEAD was 135, reduced 1, not worsened). build_rolling clean. Added test file also clean. NO new violation; not blocking run_comparison per handoff.

r4-validation.title: --utilization validated
r4-validation.imperative: choices=UTILIZATION_LEVELS, default balanced, invalid rejected with non-zero exit.
r4-validation.finding: Both scripts: argparse --utilization choices=UTILIZATION_LEVELS, default='balanced' (brc 230-235, rsrc 545-550). Invalid value -> SystemExit non-zero (tests test_main_rejects_invalid_utilization / test_parse_args_rejects_invalid_utilization green). resolve_resource_plan also re-validates level (utilization.py 130).
